enonce.texte: Match the English words with their French translations. Draw a line between the two columns.

questions.reponse: bread = pain, rice = riz, chicken = poulet, fish = poisson, water = eau, juice = jus, coffee = café, tea = thé

enonce.texte:
Classify the following foods into the correct categories: Fruits, Vegetables, Meat/Fish, or Drinks.

List: apple, carrot, chicken, orange, water, fish, tomato, banana, coffee, rice (rice can be classified as 'Other' if not fitting the four categories).

questions.reponse: Fruits: apple, orange, banana; Vegetables: carrot, tomato; Meat/Fish: chicken, fish; Drinks: water, coffee; Other: rice

enonce.texte: Answer the following questions about your meals in complete sentences using the present simple tense.

questions.texte: What do you eat for breakfast?
questions.reponse: I eat [food] for breakfast. (e.g., I eat bread and drink coffee for breakfast.)

questions.texte: What does your best friend eat for lunch?
questions.reponse: He/She eats [food] for lunch. (e.g., He eats rice and chicken for lunch.)
Yes, I like vegetables. / No, I don't like vegetables.

questions.texte: Does your mother cook dinner every day?
questions.reponse: Yes, she cooks dinner every day. / No, she doesn't cook dinner every day.

enonce.texte: Create a simple menu for a restaurant. The menu must have three categories: Starters, Main Courses, and Desserts. For each category, write two items and the price in CFA francs. Then, write a dialogue between a waiter and a customer ordering one starter, one main course, and one dessert.

questions.reponse: Menu: Starters: Salad (1000 F), Soup (800 F); Main Courses: Chicken with rice (2500 F), Fish with fries (2200 F); Desserts: Ice cream (700 F), Fruit salad (600 F). Dialogue: Waiter: Good evening! Are you ready to order? Customer: Yes, please. I would like the soup and the chicken with rice. Waiter: And for dessert? Customer: Ice cream, please. Waiter: Thank you!

enonce.texte:
Read the text and answer the questions.

My Daily Meals

Hello! My name is Amina. I live in Douala. I usually eat breakfast at 7 a.m. I eat bread and drink tea. For lunch, I eat rice and fish at noon. In the evening, I eat dinner with my family. We eat chicken and vegetables. I don't like coffee, but I love fruit juice. My brother, Ali, likes coffee and rice. He doesn't like fish.

questions.texte: What does Amina eat for breakfast?
questions.reponse: She eats bread and drinks tea.

questions.texte: What time does Amina eat lunch?

questions.reponse: Yes, they eat dinner with her family.

enonce.texte: Find and correct the mistakes in the following sentences. Some sentences may be correct.

Work with a partner. One student is the waiter, the other is the customer. Use the menu you created in the 'Creating a Menu' exercise or use the provided menu below. The waiter must greet the customer, take the order, and give the total price. The customer must order food, ask about the ingredients, and thank the waiter.

Menu: Starter: Soup (800 F), Salad (1000 F); Main: Grilled Fish (2000 F), Beef Stew (2500 F); Dessert: Fruit (500 F), Cake (700 F); Drinks: Water (300 F), Juice (500 F).

questions.texte: Write the dialogue you have with your partner.
questions.reponse: Waiter: Good evening! Welcome to our restaurant. Can I take your order? Customer: Yes, please. I would like the soup. Waiter: What would you like for the main course? Customer: I would like the grilled fish. Waiter: Do you want any drinks? Customer: Yes, I want juice. Waiter: And for dessert? Customer: Fruit, please. Waiter: Your total is 2000 + 500 + 500 = 3000 F. Thank you!
